extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: An open book question answering dataset modeled after open book exams, consisting of 5957 multiple-choice questions and a set of 1326 elementary science facts. Answering requires combining a provided science fact with additional common knowledge in a multi-hop reasoning setting.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created through a multi-stage process starting from a set of elementary science facts, then using crowdsourcing to generate questions about novel situations, followed by automatic, crowd, and expert filtering for hardness, answerability, and quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data consisted of a set of 1326 elementary-level science facts used as the open book, from which roughly 5957 multiple-choice questions were generated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-stage crowdsourced question generation and validation: a worker was shown a core science fact, asked to think of a second common fact, create a multiple-choice question with one correct and three incorrect answers, pass system checks and automatic hardness filtering, then the question was answered by 5 new crowdworkers and kept only if at least 4 of 5 answered correctly; Dev/Test were further filtered by an in-house expert.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answerability was validated by 5 crowdworker judgments per question with a 4-of-5 acceptance threshold; the paper also analyzes human performance statistically using the 5 judgments per question and Hoeffding’s Inequality.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers from North America with 'masters' level qualification
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic filtering with an information retrieval solver and a word association based solver
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes inevitable human bias from crowdsourcing, which makes the dataset partially gameable and allows simple neural baselines exploiting answer plausibility or odd-one-out patterns to achieve inflated performance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The open book facts are not self-contained and are generally insufficient by themselves to answer questions; the dataset requires additional common knowledge and multi-hop reasoning, and retrieving the needed knowledge remains an open challenge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and development of open-book question answering systems that combine core science facts with external common knowledge; Train and Dev also provide intermediate supervision via the supporting fact used to generate each question.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multi-stage crowdsourcing and filtering were used to generate and refine the dataset, including automatic hardness filtering, crowd answerability filtering, random shuffling of answer choices, and additional expert filtering for Dev/Test.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source fact set was filtered from WorldTree to central facts and then further reduced to facts general enough for multiple situations; generated questions also had to pass basic checks such as exactly four choices, no negation words, and uniform answer choice length.

name.evidence: We present a new kind of question answering dataset, OpenBookQA

description.evidence: OpenBookQA, modeled after open book exams... The open book that comes with our questions is a set of 1326 elementary level science facts. Roughly 6000 questions probe an understanding of these facts and their application to novel situations.
